attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-1
attempts.entry_title: Barrel cortex activity during tactile behavior (Peron et al. 2015)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data. The map of touch and whisking coding across layers, cell types and barrel columns, the concentration of touch neurons in the principal column, the stability of representations during learning and the map of directional tuning all need layer, cell-type or column labels that the data set does not carry. It also holds only a few sessions from three of the paper's eight mice, with no imaging during learning or under anesthesia. Of two minor behavioural details, the number of trials per session matched, while whisking amplitude fell outside the paper's range under every measure the claim names, a measure the paper does not define.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Peron, Freeman, Iyer, Guo and Svoboda (2015) on CRCNS ssc-1, which holds five imaging sessions from three of the paper's eight volume-imaging mice, with dF/F per ROI, whisker angle and curvature, touches and trial data. The trials per session and the whisking amplitude are tested. The data set has no calcium events and no layer, cell-class or column labels, and none of the learning, L4 axon or anesthetized data, so the claims on neural coding are blocked.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Peron et al. (2015) from CRCNS ssc-1

outcomes.statement: The eight volume-imaging mice have ROI counts (neurons and apical dendrites) of 11,031, 9,637, 13,788, 16,200, 8,288, 12,293, 19,012 and 18,125, with spared whiskers C2, D2, C2, D2, C3, C2, D3 and D2 (an171923, an194181, an194672, an197522, an198503, an229716, an229717, an229719).
outcomes.source: Table S1
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table S1; no sentence states them. The table text was read from the extracted supplement.
outcomes.notes: The data set holds 3 of the 8 mice (an197522, an229717, an229719), with one or two sessions each where the paper imaged about four sessions per subvolume. Distinct ROIs per mouse are 11,649, 3,771 and 11,341 against 16,200, 19,012 and 18,125 in Table S1 (72%, 20%, 63%), 26,761 in all against 108,374. The spared whiskers named in the files (D2, D3, D2) match Table S1. The count the claim tests rests on sessions that are not deposited, so it cannot be compared.

outcomes.statement: The core data set comprises 82,732 excitatory L2/3 neurons, 777 L1 neurons and 3,806 L2/3 GABAergic neurons from 8 mice, and 2,469 L5 apical dendrites imaged in deep L3.
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraphs 6 and 9; Figure 3
outcomes.quote: Our core data set comprised 82,732 excitatory L2/3 neurons, 777 L1 neurons, and 3,806 L2/3 GABAergic neurons (n = 8 mice
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). Every dF/F series is described only as "dF/F for ROIs in subvolume <n>", every idStrs entry is "dF/F Ca TS for <id>", idStrsDetailed is empty, and the ROI ids number planes, not layers or classes. The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The criterion uses the class labels the data set carries. The Gad2 mouse an194181 and four other mice are also absent; 26,761 ROIs of 3 mice are in the data set.

outcomes.statement: GABAergic neurons are 4.3% of the 86,538 L2/3 neurons recorded, about a third of those expected, so sampling of GABAergic neurons is incomplete.
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: We found 3,806 GABAergic neurons among 86,538 neurons in L2/3 (4.3%)
outcomes.notes: The only mouse with labelled GABAergic neurons, an194181 (Gad2-T2A-NLS-mCherry), is not in the data set, and no ROI carries a cell-class label.

outcomes.statement: In L2/3, 76% ± 6% of red nuclei counted in the high-resolution stacks had a corresponding ROI, and a barrel column holds 1,796 ± 299 L2/3 pyramidal neurons (n = 5 volumes).
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraph 6; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: In L2/3, 76% ± 6% of red nuclei had corresponding ROIs ... Our count for L2/3 pyramidal neurons per barrel column (1,796 ± 299; n = 5 volumes
outcomes.notes: The high-resolution reference stacks and the nucleus counts from them are not in the data set. By the data description its imaging archives hold registered trial TIFFs; the notebook does not list their contents. The criterion uses nuclei counts the data set carries and blocks the claim otherwise.

outcomes.statement: Mice reached criterion performance (d-prime > 1.5) after 11 ± 4 days of training (mean ± SD, n = 8 mice).
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraph 2; Figure 1E
outcomes.quote: Mice reached criterion level performance (d-prime > 1.5, or approximately 70% trials correct; Figure 1E) after 11 ± 4 days (mean ± SD; n = 8 mice) of training
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no training sessions, only five imaging sessions of trained mice.

outcomes.statement: Mice performed 245 ± 71 trials per session during imaging.
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Mice performed 245 ± 71 trials per session during imaging
outcomes.notes: The five sessions hold 398, 370, 184, 231 and 268 behavioural trials. Pooled over sessions the mean is 290.2 (SD 91.2), and the mean of the three per-mouse means (384.0, 184.0, 249.5) is 272.5; both are within 245 +/- 71. Counting only trials with imaging gives 238.6 pooled and 225.2 over mice. Trial ids run from 1 without gaps in every session and the imaged trials are a subset of them, consistent with tables that cover whole behavioural sessions; in each session trial 1 is followed by a pause of 12.5 min to 2.4 h, so dropping it would change each count by one. The five sessions are the only ones deposited and how they were chosen is not documented, so they may not represent the paper's imaging sessions; the agreement is weak evidence.
deviations: Five sessions of 3 of the paper's 8 mice; the paper's number covers every imaging session of 8 mice.

outcomes.statement: The task elicited larger amplitude whisker movements than similar two-position tasks, 55.5 ± 13.3 degrees (mean ± SD, n = 8 mice) against about 20 degrees.
outcomes.source: Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations in Behaving Mice, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: our task elicited larger amplitude whisker movements (approximately 20
outcomes.notes: Means over the three mice (per mouse 70.6, 99.2, 54.2 for a) are (a) 74.7 degrees for the per-trial angle range over the trial, (b) 29.0 over the sample epoch and (c) 26.9 for the peak Hilbert amplitude (6 to 30 Hz; 22.2 to 30.4 with the other bands shown); none is within 55.5 +/- 13.3 (42.2 to 68.8). Removing tracking errors brings reading (a) close to the upper bound but not inside it under any mask that removes only errors. Without samples above 85 degrees (in 26, 52 and 2 trials per mouse) reading (a) is 72.4 and without one- or two-sample spikes 71.9. It falls steadily as the threshold on the angle drops, 74.1 at 88 degrees, 72.4 at 85, 70.3 at 80 and 67.4 at 70, the lower thresholds also cutting the tops of real protractions; spike thresholds of 10 to 40 degrees give 71.7 to 72.1. Unwrapping protractions that pass 90 degrees and wrap to the other sign gives 77.0. Jumps that last three samples or more are nearly all in an229717 (99.9th percentile step 34.5 degrees per 2 ms against 4.5 to 7.0 in the other sessions; a step over 30 degrees that returns within 25 samples in 116 of its 183 trials, against 9 of 764 and 4 of 496). Removing them gives 69.7 to 70.1 over six step and duration values (69.8 at 30 degrees and 25 samples), and 69.2 with the limit and spike masks as well, 0.4 above the bound of 68.8; an229717 falls from 99.2 to 84.0 to 86.0. A 21-sample running median filter gives 68.6, and 68.3 with every other mask, inside, but it also removes real whisk peaks, flagging samples in 79 of 764 trials of an197522, whose largest steps are 9.1 to 11.3 degrees (99.99th percentile), and lowering that mouse from 70.1 to 69.0. Trials with no masked sample give 59.4 over mice, but they are a selection (in an197522 66.1 against 70.6 for all trials). The miss is therefore narrow, 0.4 to 1.3 degrees for the cleanings that remove only errors, and whether a cleaned reading (a) falls inside depends on a choice the paper does not describe. Leaving out 0.2 s at each end of the trial, where the filter's edge effect inflates a synthetic sinusoid's peak Hilbert amplitude from 20 to 22.0 (20.1 without the ends), changes reading (c) to 26.6, and 26.6 with artefacts interpolated. Reading (b) without artefacts is 28.6 to 29.0. Measures the criterion does not list fall inside the tolerance, the mean of per-mouse medians of reading (a) (68.6), the 1st to 99th percentile range of angle per trial (49.2) and twice the peak Hilbert amplitude, a peak-to-peak measure (53.7 +/- 15.7; 53.2 without ends and artefacts). The part of the statement the criterion does not test, larger movements than about 20 degrees, holds for every full-sweep measure (28.6 to 77.0). The paper does not define the measure; the question is recorded as a finding for its authors. 1,443 trials (764, 183, 496 per mouse).
deviations: Three of the paper's eight mice, five sessions.

The sample epoch is the pole-in-reach interval of the data set's poleInReach series (the paper's "1 s sample epoch (pole in reach)", Results, Imaging Large Neuronal Populations, paragraph 1). The Figure 1C legend gives the epoch as 1 to 2 s and the claims file's opening comment as 1 s; a reader is asked about the comment (questions/peron-2015.yaml). The data's intervals are used as they are, so the difference does not enter the result.

The band used to isolate whisking before the Hilbert transform (reading c) is not given in the paper or in the Supplemental Experimental Procedures, which cite Huber et al. (2012); 6 to 30 Hz is used, with 4 to 30 and 8 to 25 Hz shown. Every band gives the same outcome, so the outcome does not rest on it.

Only trials the data set lists as valid whisker trials are used. Rare angle samples at +/-90 degrees (at most 0.06% of samples), which look like tracking errors, are kept in the main readings, as the criterion's maximum minus minimum includes them. Readings (a) and (b) are also shown without samples above 85 degrees and without spikes over 20 degrees from a 5-sample running median, with other thresholds, and after unwrapping; reading (a) also without jumps of several samples (a step over 30 degrees in one sample that returns within 25 samples, with other values, and running medians of 11 and 21 samples); reading (c) without 0.2 s at each end. These are standard choices, not from the paper, which says nothing on tracking errors. Every one that removes only errors gives the same outcome; the 21-sample median, which also cuts real whisk peaks, does not (68.6, or 68.3 with every mask). The 1st to 99th percentile range is shown as a further variant.

outcomes.statement: Representation of whisking was uniform across neurons inside and outside the principal column, so touch neurons were mainly confined to the principal column while whisking neurons were spread uniformly.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Organization of Sensory Coding, paragraph 1; Figure 7C
outcomes.quote: Representation of whisking was uniform across neurons inside and outside the principal column. Thus, touch neurons were primarily confined to the principal column, whereas whisking neurons were distributed uniformly
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The data set also holds no calcium events (only dF/F), which the paper's task-related, discrimination and encoding-model criteria use (M1, M3 to M5).

outcomes.statement: Touch and whisking L2/3 neurons are intermingled; the pairwise distances among neurons of a category do not differ from those among all neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Organization of Sensory Coding, paragraphs 1 and 3; Figures 7A, 7B and S6
outcomes.quote: We found no difference when comparing the distribution of pairwise distances among neurons of a category (touch, whisking, and mixed) to the pairwise distance distribution among all neurons
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The data set also holds no calcium events (only dF/F), which the paper's task-related, discrimination and encoding-model criteria use (M1, M3 to M5). The 3D positions the pairwise distances need are not given either: ROI masks give positions within a plane, with no plane depth or offset between subvolumes.

outcomes.statement: The L2/3 neuropil signal was temporally more concentrated in the sample epoch and spatially more concentrated in the principal column than L2/3 somata.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Organization of Sensory Coding, paragraph 2; Figures 4C, 4D and S3
outcomes.quote: The neuropil signal was temporally more concentrated in the sample epoch and spatially more concentrated in the principal column
outcomes.notes: No neuropil ROIs or neuropil traces are in the data set; the session files hold dF/F of somatic ROIs only. Column labels are also absent.

outcomes.statement: The touch map of L4 axons correlated best with that of the L2/3 neuropil (r = 0.60), less with L2/3 somata (0.41), and somata with neuropil least (0.36).
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Organization of Sensory Coding, paragraph 2; Figure S5
outcomes.quote: the correlation between L4 axon and L2/3 neuropil touch maps was highest of the three possible pairings (L4-neuropil Pearson's R
outcomes.notes: The L4 axon imaging of the Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre mice (an224823, an227254, an238004) and the neuropil ROIs are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: Most L2/3 touch neurons were directionally tuned, with about equal numbers preferring protraction and retraction; tuning was typically strong (DI near 1 or -1), and few neurons were intermediate.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 2; Figure 8B
outcomes.quote: The majority of L2/3 touch neurons were directionally tuned (Figures 8A and 8B), with an approximately equal number of neurons preferring protraction and retraction. Directional tuning was typically strong ... Relatively few neurons showed an intermediate level of tuning
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The data set also holds no calcium events (only dF/F), which the paper's task-related, discrimination and encoding-model criteria use (M1, M3 to M5).

outcomes.statement: L2/3 directional tuning was stable during learning; the mean pairwise RMS difference of touch receptive fields across days (0.273, n = 118 neurons) was below the 5th percentile of the shuffled distribution (0.425) for 97.8% of neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 2; Figure S7
outcomes.quote: The difference between touch receptive fields among days (grand mean of RMS difference ... 0.273; n = 118 neurons) was below the 5th percentile of the shuffled distribution (0.425; shuffling by neuron identity) for 97.8% of the neurons examined
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no imaging during learning. Its five sessions are from 2013-03-08 and 2013-03-10 (an197522), 2013-12-01 (an229717) and 2013-12-02 and 2013-12-05 (an229719), each imaging 4 to 10 subvolumes of 15 um plane spacing, not one subvolume of 120 um spacing tracked from the start of training; there are no training-day sessions and no mouse an194181, an194672 or an198503.

outcomes.statement: Protraction-preferring touch neurons were more abundant in and near the column of the whisker anterior to the spared one, retraction-preferring neurons in and near the column of the posterior whisker, giving a trend in DI along the whisker row.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 3; Figures 8C to 8E
outcomes.quote: neurons sensitive to protraction touch were more abundant in and near the barrel column of the whisker anterior to the spared one, with retractionsensitive neurons more abundant in and near the column of the whisker posterior to the spared one
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The row axis and the principal column centre the criterion needs are not in the data set.

outcomes.statement: DI magnitudes inside and outside the principal column were similar (p = 0.333, Wilcoxon rank-sum), so the spatial trend reflects a change in preference among neurons of similar tuning strength.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: DI magnitudes inside and outside the principal column were similar (p = 0.333, Wilcoxon rank-sum test
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. Depends on fig8de-direction-topography, blocked for the same reason.

outcomes.statement: L4 axons and the L2/3 neuropil show a directional map along the row similar to that of L2/3 excitatory neurons, so the L2/3 directional topography is likely inherited from L4.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 4; Figure 8E
outcomes.quote: we observed a directional map, similar to that observed in L2/3 excitatory neurons, in the activity of both L4 axons and the L2/3 neuropil
outcomes.notes: Neither L4 axon nor neuropil ROIs are in the data set; it also depends on fig8de-direction-topography.

outcomes.statement: Different neurons encode passive deflection and active touch; only 8% of neurons with touch responses under anesthesia also responded to touch during behavior, with 6.5% expected by chance (n = 3 mice).
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 6; Figures 8G and 8H
outcomes.quote: Surprisingly, only 8% of neurons showing touch responses under anesthesia showed touch responses during behavior, with 6.5% expected by chance
outcomes.notes: The anesthetized passive-deflection imaging of mice an257218, an257219 and an257221 is not in the data set, which holds only three behaving volume-imaging mice (bucket listing, data check).

outcomes.statement: Under anesthesia, neurons showed no detectable topography of directional tuning.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraph 6; Figure 8I
outcomes.quote: we did not detect topography in directional tuning for neurons in anesthetized mice
outcomes.notes: The anesthetized passive-deflection imaging of mice an257218, an257219 and an257221 is not in the data set, which holds only three behaving volume-imaging mice (bucket listing, data check).

outcomes.statement: The neuropil remained direction selective under anesthesia, with forward deflection evoking responses in and near the column of the whisker anterior to the deflected one, as in anesthetized rats; this is the same spatial map as active protraction touch but with opposite lateral force.
outcomes.source: Results, Directional Tuning in vS1, paragraphs 5 and 7; Figures 8F, 8J and 8K
outcomes.quote: The neuropil signal was still direction selective under anesthesia (Figure 8J). Moreover, the topography of neuropil directionality under anesthesia was consistent with that observed in anesthetized rats (Kremer et al., 2011
outcomes.notes: The anesthetized passive-deflection imaging of mice an257218, an257219 and an257221 is not in the data set, which holds only three behaving volume-imaging mice (bucket listing, data check).

outcomes.statement: Without peri-somatic neuropil correction more neurons are classed as touch; the corrected fraction is consistent with electrophysiology.
outcomes.source: Figure S3D
outcomes.quote: Touch fraction among neurons without peri-somatic neuropil correction (above) and with correction (below). The bottom plot is consistent with electrophysiological results
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The criterion allows events to be extracted again, and raw ROI and neuropil fluorescence, which the session files lack, could in principle be rebuilt from the registered TIFFs (146 GB of imaging archives for five sessions, of the data set's 165 GB) with the deposited ROI masks and neuropil masks drawn again by the paper's rule; that was not attempted, since the claim would still need the L2/3 labels the data set lacks.

outcomes.statement: A correlation-based classification of the same data classifies a larger proportion of neurons as touch than the encoding model.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Applying a correlation-based approach to our data set classifies a larger proportion of neurons as touch
outcomes.notes: The data set's ROIs carry no layer, cell-class or column label, and its planes no depth or position relative to one another (data check). The claims file's shared method M6 says the claims that need these labels are blocked when the data set carries none. The data set also holds no calcium events (only dF/F), which the paper's task-related, discrimination and encoding-model criteria use (M1, M3 to M5).

outcomes.statement: On simultaneous imaging and cell-attached data from mouse visual cortex, degraded to this study's dwell time and rate, the event detector found 54% ± 10% of single action potentials at a false positive rate of 0.01 Hz (n = 7 neurons).
outcomes.source: Experimental Procedures, Calcium Imaging Analysis, paragraph after step 5
outcomes.quote: For a false-positive detection rate of 0.01 Hz, 54% ± 10% of single action potentials (mean ± SD; n = 7 neurons) were detected
outcomes.notes: The claim is data elsewhere. The paper cites the simultaneous imaging and cell-attached data of Chen et al. (2013b) without an identifier; CRCNS cai-1 holds such data (folders named GCaMP6f_11cells_Chen2013 and others). The test cannot be repeated as described. The paper does not say how the recordings were degraded to this study's dwell time and frame rate, nor the Savitzky-Golay window of the noise estimate, nor the window within which a detected event matches an action potential, nor which 7 neurons were used. Each of these sets the detection rate at a given false-positive rate, and no choice has a basis in the paper, so no reading was run.
outcomes.where: Simultaneous imaging and cell-attached data of Chen et al. (2013b), Nature 499:295-300, as the paper cites them; the paper names no archive or identifier

findings.statement: The data set holds 5 imaging sessions from 3 of the paper's 8 volume-imaging mice (an197522, an229717, an229719), with 20% to 72% of their Table S1 ROIs (26,761 of 108,374 for all eight mice). The other five mice, including the Gad2 mouse with labelled GABAergic neurons, the imaging during learning, the L4 axon mice, the anesthetized mice, the L5 soma and dendrite pairs, the training sessions and the high-resolution reference stacks are not in it, although the paper says the data set includes the imaging data of Table S1.

The data description lists raw fluorescence and algorithmically extracted calcium events for each ROI, and files named vol_xxx holding multi-session data. The session files hold only dF/F (dffTSA) and whisker variables as time series, and no vol_xxx file exists; the imaging archives hold registered TIFFs.

No ROI carries a layer (L1, L2/3, L5 apical dendrite), cell-class or barrel-column label, and no imaging plane carries a depth or position relative to the others. The description says laminar boundaries were drawn in the reference stack, but neither the boundaries nor the stack are deposited, so the paper's comparisons between layers, classes and principal and surround columns cannot be made from the data set.

One subvolume (an197522, 2013-03-08, dffTSA 10, raw folder fov_04001, 202 ROIs) is a single plane imaged at 29 Hz, not three planes at 7 Hz as the description says of every subvolume; and many 7 Hz subvolumes have ROIs on only one or two of their three planes. Neither is described.

The event series structure is named eventSeriesArrayHash in the files, not eventSeriesHash as described; the file an229717_2013_12_01/an229717_2013_12_01_sesssion.mat has a misspelt name; the description's citation of the paper is a placeholder ("Article title. Journal Name xxx").

In an197522 on 2013-03-10 the dF/F response to the first touch is not larger with the true touch times than with the times shifted by 3 s (3 of 9 subvolumes; median 0.0009 against 0.0083 dF/F), so that session's imaging could not be shown to share the trial clock. In the other four sessions the true alignment gives the largest response in 21 of 25 subvolumes.

The whisker angle holds tracking errors that the description does not mention. Samples jump to the tracker's +/-90 degree limit for one or two samples (for example 87.3, 37.8, -89.2, 41.7 degrees on successive 2 ms samples in an229717), jump to a distant value for three samples or more (-24.1, 72.8, 72.8, 72.1, -23.1 in an229719; in an229717 a step over 30 degrees that returns within 25 samples occurs in 116 of 183 trials, and its 99.9th percentile step is 34.5 degrees against 4.5 to 7.0 in the other sessions), and protractions past 90 degrees wrap to the other sign (84.6, 89.2, -87.5, -88.7, 89.3 in an197522). Samples above 85 degrees occur in 26 of 764, 52 of 183 and 2 of 496 valid whisker trials of an197522, an229717 and an229719. The largest per-trial angle range, 179.8 degrees, spans these limits.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the whisker movement amplitude of 55.5 +/- 13.3 degrees (Results, paragraph 2) measured? On the three mice in the data set the per-trial angle range is 74.7 degrees (69.2 without the tracking errors), its range over the sample epoch 29.0, and the peak Hilbert amplitude 26.9 (6 to 30 Hz band, also not given), while twice the peak Hilbert amplitude is 53.7. Which measure, epoch and band were used, and how were tracking errors handled?

Question for the paper's authors. For the event detector's validation (54% of single action potentials at 0.01 Hz false positives, n = 7), which recordings of Chen et al. (2013) were used, how were they degraded to this study's dwell time and frame rate, and what were the Savitzky-Golay window and the matching window?

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module ssc1.py and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive listing (146 files, 165 GB) and tested whisking_amplitudes on synthetic inputs; it downloaded no data. Its report gave its own outcome for each claim; 42 of 43 agree with the record. Problem 6 (the sample epoch's length in the claims file's opening comment) is asked of a reader in questions/peron-2015.yaml. Report in transcripts/peron-2015/verifier-1-report.md.

disagreements.reason: None of the three listed readings lands in [42.2, 68.8]. They give (a) 74.7, (b) 29.0 and (c) 26.9. Two unlisted variants do. The 1-99 percentile range gives 49.2 and 2 x the Hilbert peak gives 53.7. Reading (a) is inflated by +/-90 degree tracking errors; one +/-90 pair turns a 40 degree range into 180, the per-trial maximum is 179.8, and fixing this needs a reading (a) that drops only the artefact samples (problem 1). The per-trial maximum of the Hilbert amplitude over the whole trial is inflated by filter and Hilbert edge effects, about 10% on a clean sinusoid, and by artefact spikes, so the passing 2 x Hilbert variant is biased upward (problem 2). The qualitative part, well above about 20 degrees, holds for every full-sweep measure. Under the strict criterion the outcome would be not_reproduced (problem 3). n = 3 of 8 mice.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the first revision, the helper module ssc1.py, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. Its report agrees with all 43 outcomes; it asked for reading (a) without multi-sample tracking jumps and corrections to sentences the numbers did not support. It found no misreading of the paper in the claims file (the degree values it calls garbled are legible apart from the degree signs, which does not affect the criterion), so no question was added. Report in transcripts/peron-2015/verifier-2-report.md.

entries.name: peron-2015
entries.title: Barrel cortex activity during tactile behavior (Peron et al. 2015)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Peron, Freeman, Iyer, Guo and Svoboda (2015) on CRCNS ssc-1, which holds five imaging sessions from three of the paper's eight volume-imaging mice, with dF/F per ROI, whisker angle and curvature, touches and trial data. The trials per session and the whisking amplitude are tested. The data set has no calcium events and no layer, cell-class or column labels, and none of the learning, L4 axon or anesthetized data, so the claims on neural coding are blocked.
